title: Seamless Phase 1/2 and Phase 2/3 Trial Designs: FDA Precedents and Reviewer Requirements
summary: FDA precedents for seamless Phase 1/2 and Phase 2/3 trials in drugs and biologics, and what reviewers required on dose selection, adaptation rules and type I error.
body_markdown:
## FDA acceptance of seamless Phase 1/2 and Phase 2/3 designs: precedents and reviewer requirements


FDA has accepted seamless designs in drug and biologic programs when the dose-selection stage, the adaptation rules and the confirmatory inference were planned in advance and protected from operational bias. The review record shows a consistent pattern. FDA is generally willing to let one protocol carry a program from dose finding into confirmation. What it negotiates is which patients count toward confirmatory efficacy, how the selected dose was chosen, and how the familywise type I error rate survives the selection step.


### Key takeaways


- FDA's final adaptive design guidance (November 2019) states that seamless designs combining dose selection and confirmation of efficacy using data from the entire trial "can be considered," provided its adaptive-design principles are followed[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=275)[276](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=276) .
- Accepted Phase 2/3 precedents in Drugs@FDA and CBER review files include sarilumab (KEVZARA), dulaglutide (TRULICITY), propranolol oral solution (HEMANGEOL), risdiplam (EVRYSDI), nivolumab/relatlimab (OPDUALAG) and the 9-valent HPV vaccine (GARDASIL 9)[232](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=232)[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=62)[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=77)[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=66)[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=69)[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=297)[150](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=150) .
- FDA often accepted the operational seamlessness while limiting the inferential seamlessness. For TRULICITY it treated only Stage 2 as confirmatory[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=75) , and for KEVZARA it excluded the pre-selection Part B cohort from efficacy analyses[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=229)[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=230) .
- Where stages were combined inferentially, reviewers expected a prespecified testing method that accounts for the selection step and controls multiplicity. HEMANGEOL used a weighted inverse-normal combination function with Simes adjustment and closed testing[330](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=330)[334](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=334) .
- Recurring reviewer requests: prespecified selection rules and simulations, a single endpoint for selection and confirmation (STELARA proposal), a broad enough dose range, firewalls documenting "who knows what," and justification for pooling stages[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=87)[240](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=240)[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=101)[96](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=96)[95](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=95) .


### What FDA guidance says


#### Adaptive design guidance (final, 2019)


The *Adaptive Designs for Clinical Trials of Drugs and Biologics* guidance addresses seamless designs under "Adaptations to Treatment Arm Selection," not as a separate Phase 2/3 category[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=275)[276](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=276) . It distinguishes adaptive dose-ranging intended to pick doses for a future confirmatory trial from in-trial arm selection intended to provide substantial evidence of effectiveness[277](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=277) . Its central requirements are:


- Prospective specification of both the treatment-arm selection rule and the testing method, along with rules for any other interim modification[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=275)[281](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=281) .
- Testing that accounts for selecting the best dose(s) from several evaluated doses and for additional adaptations such as early stopping or sample-size changes. Group-sequential methods can be combined with a multiple-testing approach that controls type I error across doses[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=275)[285](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=285) .
- Limiting access to comparative interim results and ensuring timely, reliable interim data[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=288)[289](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=289) .
- Use of analytical methods that avoid biased estimates, with simulations often critical for complex designs[294](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=294) .
- Unplanned changes based on comparative interim results can undermine type I error control and are strongly discouraged without first meeting FDA[284](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=284) .


#### ICH E20 draft (September 2025)


The draft *E20 Adaptive Designs for Clinical Trials* guidance, section 4.4 "Treatment Selection," describes selecting one or both doses at interim and assessing efficacy and benefit-risk using both stages. Planning should specify the treatments, interim decisions, anticipated selection rules, effects on randomization and sample size, and management of participants on a discontinued treatment[249](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=249) . Sponsors should ensure interim estimates support reliable selection, including appropriate interim timing[278](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=278) . E20 generally recommends statistical methods that allow departure from the anticipated selection rule so the full interim information can inform the decision[282](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=282)[283](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=283) . It also warns that selecting treatments with more favorable interim results biases conventional end-of-trial estimates, and that sponsors should consider adjusted estimates[292](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=292)[293](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=293) . Operationally, it calls for limiting what can be inferred from interim analyses and for prespecified randomization algorithms with minimal sponsor involvement[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=256) .


#### Oncology dosage optimization (final, August 2024)


The *Optimizing the Dosage of Human Prescription Drugs and Biological Products for the Treatment of Oncologic Diseases* guidance describes a "seamless approach" with rapid transitions from dose finding to registration trials and states that, with sufficient planning, dosage optimization can be aligned with expedited development[1](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=1)[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=6) . A registration trial comparing multiple dosages with a control should provide strong control of type I error, with a multiple-testing procedure covering both the multiple treatment comparisons and the interim assessments at which inferior arms are dropped[286](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=286) . Dosage-arm enrollment may be stopped at interim after review of activity and/or safety, and selection should compare exposure, dose interruptions and reductions, discontinuations and serious adverse reactions across dosages[279](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=279)[280](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=280) . Inadequately justified dose selection can raise clinical-hold concerns[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=9) .


#### Expansion cohorts in first-in-human oncology trials (final, March 2022)


For Phase 1/2-style programs, the *Expansion Cohorts: Use in First-in-Human Clinical Trials to Expedite Development of Oncology Drugs and Biologics* guidance describes concurrently accruing cohorts that assess safety, pharmacokinetics and antitumor activity within a single FIH trial[13](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=13)[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=28) . It covers drug characteristics suited to the approach, the information needed to support each cohort, and when to interact with FDA[30](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=30)[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=38) . The separate master protocols guidance explicitly excludes FIH expansion-cohort trials from its scope[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=31)[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=32) .


A related note for device-adjacent readers: FDA's 2016 device adaptive design guidance explicitly permits inferentially seamless feasibility-to-pivotal studies if the combination plan precedes unblinded access to feasibility data and controls overall type I error across both stages. That is device guidance, not a drug or biologic rule[287](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=287) .


### Phase 2/3 precedents in FDA review records


Product (application) Trial Seamless structure Dose selection Type I error / inference approach FDA position


KEVZARA, sarilumab (BLA 761037) EFC11072 Operationally seamless Phase 2/3: Part A dose ranging, Part B confirmation without recruitment interruption[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=225)[226](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=226) Six-arm Part A; 150 mg and 200 mg q2w selected on efficacy and safety[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=227)[319](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=319) Only Part B Cohort 2 in efficacy ITT; Bonferroni across two doses, hierarchical testing at α = 0.025 per dose[320](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=320)[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=321)[323](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=323) FDA agreed to the design, subject to excluding Cohort B1 from efficacy[232](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=232)[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=229)


TRULICITY, dulaglutide (BLA 125469) GBCF Adaptive dose-finding, "inferentially seamless" Phase 2/3[235](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=235) Bayesian adaptive allocation across seven doses using a clinical utility index; 1.5 mg and 0.75 mg selected[235](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=235)[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=236) FDA would treat only Stage 2 as confirmatory because of selection bias[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=75) Clinical reviewer: dose-selection process "seems acceptable"[351](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=351)


HEMANGEOL, propranolol (NDA 205410) Study 201 Two-stage adaptive seamless Phase II/III[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=77) IDMC selected 3 mg/kg/day for 6 months from four regimens[332](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=332)[333](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=333) Weighted inverse-normal combination of stage p-values, Simes adjustment, one-sided ≤0.005; closed testing for key secondary[330](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=330)[334](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=334) Clinical and statistical reviewers agreed data supported approval[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=81)


EVRYSDI, risdiplam (NDA 213535) FIREFISH, SUNFISH Two-part "operationally seamless" Phase 2/3 studies[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=66)[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=69) Part 1 dose escalation selected the Part 2 dose[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=66)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=223) For the original 2020 approval, FDA based SUNFISH efficacy on Part 2 and FIREFISH efficacy on Part 1[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=71) Efficacy determinations made on the stated parts[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=71)[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=68)


OPDUALAG, nivolumab/relatlimab (BLA 761234) CA224047 Adaptive Phase 2/3 with prespecified PFS HR ≤0.8 gate to full Phase 3[212](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=212)[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=297) Not a dose-selection design; Phase 2 to Phase 3 go decision on DMC recommendation[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=297) Phase 2 participants included in Phase 3 analyses; stage-wise alpha allocation not detailed in the cited review pages[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=297)[295](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=295) FDA called the trial well designed and well conducted[106](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=106)[107](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=107)


GARDASIL 9, 9vHPV vaccine (BLA 125508) V503-001 Seamless Phase IIb/III adaptive design[149](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=149)[150](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=150) Part A compared three formulations on immunogenicity; one carried into Part B[122](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=122)[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=151) Final one-sided alpha 0.0247 for GMT noninferiority, analogous to spending ≤0.001 at interim (Haybittle-Peto)[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=152) Reviewer noted sponsor trial staff did not see unblinded Part A data; blinding preserved[155](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=155)


#### KEVZARA: operational seamlessness without pooled inference


EFC11072 moved from Part A (Phase 2 dose ranging) into Part B (Phase 3) without a recruitment pause, and the clinical reviewer classified it as not an adaptive design: Part A was the learning stage, Part B the confirmatory stage[226](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=226)[318](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=318) . Part A patients did not enter Part B[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=227) . Because Part B enrollment began before dose selection, Cohort 1 was initially randomized across all six arms; patients on unselected doses were discontinued after selection[228](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=228)[320](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=320) . FDA required that Cohort 1 be excluded from efficacy and retained for safety, and the pivotal efficacy population was Cohort 2's 1,197 randomized patients[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=229)[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=230)[322](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=322) . The dose rationale combined efficacy across four regimens with dose-related discontinuations and neutrophil reductions, favoring the lowest effective regimen plus 200 mg q2w[319](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=319) . Familywise error was held at two-sided 5% using a Bonferroni split across doses and a four-step endpoint hierarchy[323](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=323)[324](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=324) .


#### TRULICITY: a Bayesian selection stage treated as exploratory


GBCF used adaptive allocation and Bayesian predictive probabilities across seven weekly doses (0.25 to 3.0 mg), with selection driven by a clinical utility index combining HbA1c, weight, diastolic blood pressure and heart rate[235](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=235) . The decision point was data-driven rather than calendar-fixed[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=73) . A lower dose had to have acceptable utility and be ≤50% of the maximum-utility dose[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=236) . At FDA's recommendation, a second, lower dose was carried forward in case a safety signal emerged at the maximum-utility dose[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=62) . Although the sponsor's analyses pooled both stages, FDA had stated in January 2008 correspondence that it would consider only Stage 2 confirmatory and Stage 1 exploratory because of potential selection bias[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=73)[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=75) .


#### HEMANGEOL: a full inferentially seamless design and the questions it raised


Study 201 is the clearest example in the record of a sponsor-planned stage-combined confirmatory analysis. The interim analysis was planned after 40 patients per active regimen and 20 placebo patients completed Week 24, with one or two regimens allowed to advance[330](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=330)[331](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=331) . Stage 1 and Stage 2 p-values were combined with a weighted inverse-normal function, Simes' method adjusted the Stage 1 p-value, and type I error was held at one-sided ≤0.005[330](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=330) . Patients already on unselected regimens stayed on treatment but were excluded from the primary analysis[338](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=338) .


During IND review, FDA asked whether controlling error conditional on selecting one versus two doses would control the unconditional study-wise error rate, requested a detailed multiplicity plan, and asked what could be claimed if primary and key secondary endpoints succeeded at different doses[185](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=185) . Reviewers also questioned the ambiguous "best regimen" rule, how IDMC clinicians would resolve disagreements, why a second regimen might be selected, and why randomization ratios were not prespecified[182](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=182)[183](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=183) . They requested the timing and rules for any second-stage sample-size increase and firewall procedures[184](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=184) . At the NDA stage, the clinical reviewer observed that randomization to all five arms had finished before the January 2012 interim meeting and questioned whether a seamless adaptive design had been necessary at all[79](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=79) . FDA's statistical reviewer likewise said that, because all five arms were fully randomized before the interim analysis, the trial should be analyzed as a conventional five-arm parallel trial with an unblinded interim analysis, and noted that differential dropout probably left the nominal p-value overstating the strength of evidence. Reviewers nonetheless agreed the data supported approval[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=81) .


#### GARDASIL 9: a seamless vaccine program at CBER


V503-001 randomized about 1,240 subjects in Part A across three 9vHPV formulations and the quadrivalent control, then selected one formulation on interim immunogenicity for Part B's approximately 13,380 subjects[122](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=122) . Part A subjects on the selected formulation or control continued into the efficacy substudy[123](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=123)[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=151) . The statistical reviewer recorded that Merck personnel involved in trial conduct did not view unblinded Part A data during selection, so selected-dose and control participants could continue into Phase III without compromising blinding[155](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=155) . Alpha for the Part B GMT noninferiority test was adjusted to a nominal one-sided 0.0247 to account for the interim look[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=152) .


### Phase 1/2 and Phase 1/2/3 designs


The review record for combined Phase 1/2 trials looks different from Phase 2/3. These trials are usually single-arm oncology or cell and gene therapy studies, and FDA's comments focus on dose rationale and interpretability rather than familywise error control.


- **COMIRNATY (BLA 125742)** : Study C4591001 was explicitly Phase 1/2/3, testing 10, 20 and 30 µg in Phase 1 and carrying 30 µg into Phase 2/3[442](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=442) .
- **BREYANZI (BLA 125714)** : Study 017001 was described by the statistical reviewer as a "seamless designed, Phase 1 study," with dose finding, dose escalation/expansion, and dose confirmation at the regimen selected by a Steering Committee using a modified continual reassessment method[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=159)[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=161)[162](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=162) . The 100 × 10⁶ CAR+ T-cell dose was chosen from cumulative efficacy and safety data[434](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=434) .
- **EPKINLY (BLA 761324)** : GCT3013-01 was a Phase 1/2 dose escalation and expansion trial, and FDA based its core efficacy assessment on the expansion cohort[383](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=383)[393](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=393) . FDA described the evidence as open-label, multi-cohort and single-arm[384](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=384) .
- **JIDEYTRO (NDA 220185)** : ARROS-1 combined BOIN dose escalation, expansion at candidate RP2Ds and Phase 2 cohorts; FDA used patients treated at 100 mg once daily as its primary efficacy population[380](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=380)[386](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=386) . FDA noted that in a single-arm trial efficacy is judged on response magnitude, precision and duration rather than inferential testing[397](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=397) .
- **BEQALZI (NDA 220711)** : Study 201 was reviewed as a pivotal Phase 1/2 study with dose escalation and safety expansion in Part 1 and efficacy expansion in Part 2; the safety monitoring committee determined the RP2D from Part 1 data[387](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=387)[389](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=389) .
- **AUGTYRO (NDA 218213)** : for TRIDENT-1, described in a sponsor question as "registrational Phase 1/2," FDA requested that all dosed Phase 1/2 patients be included in ORR analyses and reserved judgment on which cohorts supported approval[404](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=404) .


The review pages cited here for these programs do not contain explicit FDA findings on dose-selection adequacy or postmarketing dose-optimization requirements. Readers evaluating a Phase 1/2 registrational strategy should review the full clinical pharmacology and multidisciplinary reviews for each product.


### What FDA reviewers required


#### Dose selection


- **Same endpoint for selection and confirmation.** In a ustekinumab (STELARA) seamless proposal, Part 1 would select doses on Week 6 CDAI change while Part 2 confirmed on Week 6 clinical response; FDA recommended a single endpoint for both[240](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=240) . FDA also questioned whether time savings remained once pre-selection Part 2 patients were excluded, and suggested separate Phase 2 and Phase 3 studies[241](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=241)[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=242)[243](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=243) .
- **Adequate dose range and prespecification before the learning stage.** For resmetirom (REZDIFFRA), FDA rejected a dose rationale because Phase 2 had not identified an optimal dose, considered 80 to 100 mg too narrow, and offered a seamless Phase 2b/3/4 study as an alternative only if the entire SAP was specified before Phase 2b began[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=101)[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=102) .
- **Hedge doses.** FDA asked that TRULICITY carry a lower dose forward in case of a safety signal at the maximum-utility dose[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=62) .
- **Dose optimization before registration in oncology.** For iberdomide (ZENBEXUS), FDA raised concerns at a September 2021 meeting about a proposed 1.6 mg dose and recommended further dose optimization[345](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=345) . The sponsor redesigned CC-220-MM-002 from a single-stage Phase 3 into a two-stage inferentially seamless design in which Stage 1 compared 1, 1.3 and 1.6 mg and the IDMC selected 1 mg as the recommended Phase 3 dose[343](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=343)[354](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=354)[355](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=355) .


#### Adaptation rules and documentation


- For the methylnaltrexone (RELISTOR) seamless Phase 2/3 proposal, FDA said acceptability could not be judged without a detailed SAP that set explicit criteria for each adaptation, explained familywise type I error control and supplied simulation results[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=87) . It also requested a flowchart of the adaptations and rules, DMC charter and SAP, and documented firewalls between the sponsor, DMC and external statistical center[88](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=88)[181](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=181) . FDA questioned why sponsor non-project clinicians and statisticians needed to join DMC dose-selection deliberations[86](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=86) .
- For HEMANGEOL, FDA asked for a clear "best regimen" definition and prespecified randomization ratios for the confirmatory stage[182](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=182)[183](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=183) .


#### Type I error control and pooling of stages


FDA handled the selection-stage data in three ways:


1. **Exclude pre-selection data from confirmatory efficacy.** This applied to TRULICITY Stage 1[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=75) and KEVZARA Part B Cohort 1[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=229)[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=321) , and, in a proposal, STELARA's pre-selection Part 2 patients[241](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=241) .
2. **Combine stages with a prespecified adaptive test.** HEMANGEOL used an inverse-normal combination function with Simes and closed testing, and FDA probed whether unconditional study-wise error was controlled[330](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=330)[334](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=334)[185](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=185) .
3. **Pool with justification and stage-specific sensitivity analyses.** For ZENBEXUS, FDA required justification for pooling, comparison of demographics and baseline characteristics before versus after dose selection, and separate efficacy analyses by enrollment stage[95](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=95) . FDA's assessment reported a one-sided type I error of 0.005 for the MRD-negative CR endpoint[246](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=246) .


Alpha recycling across phases also drew scrutiny: in the REZDIFFRA proposal, FDA warned that failure of any hierarchically tested Phase 3 key secondary endpoint would mean that Phase 3 alpha could not be recycled to Phase 4 primary endpoints[103](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=103) .


#### Firewalls and interim data access


FDA consistently tied acceptability to documented information control. For ZENBEXUS, unblinding the study team to the Stage 1 dose-justification package was reasonable only with an adequate firewall against unintended efficacy unblinding and prespecified documentation of who would know what[96](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=96) . GARDASIL 9's reviewer specifically recorded that sponsor trial staff were walled off from unblinded Part A data[155](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=155) . The 2019 guidance and E20 draft treat this as a core design element, not an operational detail[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=288)[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=256) .


### Practical implications for sponsors


- Decide early whether the design is operationally or inferentially seamless. The precedents show FDA readily accepting operational seamlessness (KEVZARA, EVRYSDI) and expecting, for inferential seamlessness, a prespecified testing method that accounts for dose selection (HEMANGEOL's combination test) and, for complex designs, simulation results (RELISTOR)[232](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=232)[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=71)[330](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=330)[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=87) .
- Expect FDA to ask whether the seamless design actually saves time once excluded cohorts are accounted for[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=242)[243](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=243)[79](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=79) .
- Write the selection rule, the selection endpoint, the number of doses that may advance and the randomization ratio after selection into the protocol and SAP before the first interim look[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=275)[281](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=281)[183](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=183)[240](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=240) .
- Plan for estimation bias in the selected arm, not only type I error control[292](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=292)[293](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=293)[294](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=294) .
- In oncology, align the seamless dose-selection stage with the 2024 dosage optimization guidance, including strong type I error control when multiple dosages enter a registration trial[286](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=286)[279](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-acceptance-of-seamless-phase-12-and-phase-23?showSourceNumber=279) .
